column1: # Module 05 — git properly. Format: Text<TAB>tags. Card law: anki/CARD-RULES.md
A commit = {{c1::snapshot of ALL files + parent pointer(s) + message}} — never {{c2::a diff}}.
A branch = {{c1::a movable sticky note on ONE commit}} — creating one copies nothing.
HEAD = {{c1::where you're standing}} — committing moves the branch note forward.
Staging area/index = {{c1::the loading dock: exactly what the next snapshot contains}}.
git diff = {{c1::working tree vs index}}; --staged = {{c2::index vs last commit}}.
A merge commit has {{c1::TWO parents}}.
Fast-forward happens when {{c1::the target never diverged}} — note slides, no new commit.
Rebase {{c1::REPLAYS commits as new snapshots on the target}} — {{c2::new IDs; originals live in reflog}}.
Iron rebase rule: never rebase {{c1::commits others already have}}.
Undo a PUSHED bad commit: {{c1::git revert HASH}} — always safe.
History-REWRITING undo tools (local-only): {{c1::reset}} · {{c2::rebase}} · {{c3::commit --amend}}.
Lost and broken — first command: {{c1::git reflog}} (~90 days of everywhere HEAD has been).
Staged the wrong file: {{c1::git restore --staged FILE}}
fetch = {{c1::update your copy of the remote, touch nothing}}; pull = {{c2::fetch + merge/rebase}}.
dev/brain/~/.claude have NO remotes because {{c1::doctrine never leaves the machine (estate law)}}.
dev/brain keep .git OUTSIDE OneDrive because {{c1::syncing thousands of hash files corrupts/slows}}.
The 04/08 atlas incident: {{c1::an every-5-min pull --rebase replayed the branch mid-merge}} (ledger 108).
Read a repo's shape: {{c1::git log --oneline --graph --all}}
git -C PATH = {{c1::run git as if standing in PATH}}.
git stash {{c1::parks half-done work}}; get it back: {{c2::git stash pop}}.
